residency.test: Statutory Residence Test - automatic overseas tests, then automatic UK tests, then the sufficient ties test.
residency.automatic_uk: 183 days or more in the UK in the tax year, or a UK home occupied for 91 days, or full-time UK work.
residency.split_year: Available in defined cases so that only part of the year is taxed as resident.
residency.domicile: The remittance basis for non-domiciled residents was abolished from 6 April 2025 and replaced by a four-year foreign income and gains regime for new arrivals.
residency.tax_year_note: The UK tax year runs 6 April to 5 April, not the calendar year.

headline.personal_allowance: 12,570, withdrawn at 1 for every 2 of income above 100,000
headline.rates: 20% basic, 40% higher, 45% additional (Scotland has six bands up to 48%)

income_tax.name: UK income tax
income_tax.note: bands applied to income after the personal allowance; the 45% threshold is 125,140 of taxable income because the allowance is fully withdrawn by that point

personal_allowance.name: Personal allowance
personal_allowance.note: the taper creates a 60% effective marginal rate between 100,000 and 125,140

employee.name: National Insurance Class 1
employee.note: 2% applies above 50,270 and is added separately

SCT.name: Scotland
SCT.note: Scottish rates apply to non-savings, non-dividend income of Scottish taxpayers

capital_gains.rates: 18% within the basic rate band, 24% above, for both property and other assets
capital_gains.principal_residence: private residence relief usually exempts a main home
capital_gains.reporting: UK residential property disposals must be reported and paid within 60 days

quirks: The tax year is 6 April to 5 April. Reporting a calendar year by mistake is the single most common error made by people arriving from other countries.
Between 100,000 and 125,140 the personal allowance withdrawal produces a 60% effective marginal rate. Pension contributions in that band are unusually valuable.
The High Income Child Benefit Charge claws back child benefit between 60,000 and 80,000 of adjusted net income, and it is charged on the higher earner.
Most employees never file a return - PAYE settles the liability. Filing is triggered by specific circumstances such as self-employment, high income or untaxed income.
The remittance basis ended on 6 April 2025; new arrivals now use the four-year FIG regime instead, which works quite differently.

reporting.who_must_file: Self-employed with turnover above 1,000; partners in a partnership; those with untaxed income, capital gains above the exempt amount, income over 150,000, or liable to the High Income Child Benefit Charge.

deadlines.what: Register for Self Assessment for the 2025/26 tax year
Online return and balancing payment for 2025/26
UK residential property capital gains return

forms.name: End of year employment certificate (from employer)

documents_to_collect: P11D for benefits in kind such as a company car or medical insurance
Records of Gift Aid donations and personal pension contributions - both extend the basic rate band
Rental income and allowable expense records

penalties.late_filing: 100 immediately, then 10 per day after 3 months, then 5% or 300 at 6 and 12 months
penalties.late_payment: 5% of the outstanding tax at 30 days, 6 months and 12 months
penalties.interest: charged daily from the due date at the HMRC late payment rate

sources.name: GOV.UK - Income tax rates and allowances

warnings: Savings and dividend income use separate rates and allowances that this model does not apply.
Salary sacrifice, pension relief and the High Income Child Benefit Charge materially change the answer for many taxpayers.
